stale: This page is newer than the studio server: it was started before an update and lacks the new features. Run folivox ui --restart (or press Ctrl+C in its terminal and start it again).
app.tagline: local audiobook generator — everything stays on this computer
s1.drop: Drop an FB2, EPUB, DOCX, PDF, TXT or ZIP file here, or click to choose
s1.cover.hint: JPEG, PNG or WebP (or drop it here). It is saved in the audiobook file and shrunk to at most 1600 px wide.
s1.meta.sub: title, author, narrator, series… as shown in the player
s1.m.title: Title
s1.m.author: Author
s1.m.reset: Reset to the book's own data
s1.m.note: Saved automatically for this book. The series is written as the “Grouping” tag (“Name #2”), which most audiobook apps show as the series. Empty fields fall back to the book's data.
s1.pron.sub: names and invented words, read your way
s1.pron.help: One entry per line: word = how to read it. Respell the word the way it sounds (Kvothe = Quothe). A * at the end keeps any ending (Tolkien* = Tolkeen). Lines starting with # are comments.
s1.pron.forms: Enter each form of a word yourself (Mirandel, Mirandels): the stress can move between forms. Use * only for names whose stem does not change.
s1.pron.stress: Stress: + before the stressed vowel (Mir+andel) or ' right after it (Mira'ndel). Russian works the same way and also takes one capital letter. Check it by ear: the model does not always follow.
s1.pron.phon: Local engine only: phonemes between slashes, then a respelling for online engines (Kvothe = /K W OW1 TH/ | Quothe). Online engines ignore stress marks and phonemes.
s1.pron.ph:
# word = how to read it
Mirandel = Mir+andel
Kvothe = Quothe
Tolkien* = Tolkeen
s1.pron.note: Saved automatically for this book. Only the fragments with changed words are read again.
s1.pron.pick.t: Finds sentences of the book that contain your words, in the order of your list
s1.pron.sample.ph: Type a sentence with your words, or press “Pick sentences from my book”
s1.pron.try.note: This exact text is read with your pronunciations applied, using the voice and engine chosen below. It takes about half a minute and is not added to the audiobook (an online engine bills this small test).
s1.pron.needwords: Add a pronunciation to the list first.
s1.pron.missing: Not found in the book, read on their own: {words}
s1.pron.listen.t: Reads the text above with your pronunciations applied
s4.saved.sub: · kept in your account, free to reuse · click a name to rename
s4.desc.ph: a calm, warm middle-aged woman, unhurried audiobook narrator
s4.keep: Keep this voice for other books (otherwise it is deleted after this book)
s4.own: The voice I select in the list below is my own, or I have the speaker's permission to clone it. The clone exists in the provider's account while the book is made, then it is deleted.
s4.search.ph: Search voices — name, id, language, license
s4.gen.sub: an online service reads a short text (a few cents, once); you then use it for free, offline
s4.add.sub: upload a recording or record one
s4.add.rules: 6–15 s of clean speech: no music, no noise, an even calm pace
av.drop: Drop an audio file or click to choose
av.dn.sub: Gentle and for steady noise only (hiss, hum, fans). Play the sample with and without it and keep what sounds natural.
av.name: Name
av.tr: Transcript <small>(exactly what is said · empty = recognised by Whisper)</small>
av.consent: This is my own voice, or I have the speaker's permission to clone it.
gp.intro: What is this for? Folivox reads your book on this computer with a voice cloned from a short sample. No good recording? An online voice service can make that sample for you — one clip of about 10 seconds, not the whole book. You listen to a few attempts and keep the best.
gp.key.note: Stored in your OS keychain, never in a file; it is not shown again. Or set the variable in the environment before starting folivox ui.
gp.model.ph: model id exactly as the provider names it
gp.model.note: Auto asks the provider for its newest model each time. Short samples are cheap, so the best model is the sensible default.
gp.desc: Describe the voice <small>(English works best; describe a type of voice, never a real person)</small>
gp.desc.ph: e.g. a calm, warm woman in her forties, low timbre, unhurried pace, like an audiobook narrator
gp.own: This is my own voice, or I have the speaker's permission to clone it. The clone exists in the provider's account only while the takes are made, then it is deleted.
gp.text.ph: Type or paste the text to be spoken
gp.copy: Edit a copy in “My own text”
gp.ack: I understand that this short text is sent to the provider and billed to my account, and I will check the provider's terms before using the audio. Generated voices stay on this computer and are free to use; the license note under the name says what the audio may be used for.
gp.takes.note: Best match first (checked by speech recognition). Play each one and pick the voice you like — the score only says how clearly it was read.
gp.more.note: More attempts are added to the list (billed again).
run.ack: I understand that the book text is sent to this online service and billed to my account at the price above. I will check the provider's terms (terms) before sharing or selling the audio. A 600-character preview costs a few cents: try it first.
opt.ru.title: Helps the local model read Russian: it restores the letter ё (так «все» и «всё» читаются по-разному) and can add stress marks.
opt.takes.title: How many times a fragment may be re-read when speech recognition finds missing or wrong words
opt.qa.on: on: listen back with speech recognition
adv.sub: helpers that run on this computer · API keys for online providers
adv.helpers.sub: Work behind the scenes and run free on this computer; a choice marked cloud sends data to an online service and costs money. Who reads the book is chosen in step 3.
adv.diag.note: Versions, system and progress counters only: no API keys, no book text. Look inside before sharing.
adv.keys.sub: One place for the keys of the online providers you use. Which provider reads the book or makes a voice is chosen in steps 3 and 4; the keys are only needed there. Without keys the app works fully on this computer. Keys are kept in your computer's keychain, never in a file, and are never shown again.

mode.design.h: ✨ Create a voice from a description

mode.clone.s: Only your own voice, or one you have permission for.

gp.hint.clone: Copy one of your own recorded voices
gp.langhint.cartesia: Cartesia voices belong to a language: the list below shows the voices for this one.
gp.langhint: Every voice can read any language, but a ready-made voice keeps its own accent. For the most natural result in the book's language, describe a native speaker of it.

gp.freesample: Samples are provided free of charge by the service.

kind.tts.s: Reads the whole book aloud in the voice you chose. This is the heavy work and it runs on your computer.
kind.asr.s: Listens to every fragment after it is read and asks for a retake when words were misread. Also writes down your voice samples.
kind.llm.s: A language model that writes voice descriptions and picks easy passages from your book for voice samples. Optional.
kind.voicegen.s: Used by “folivox voices design” in the terminal. On this page, voice samples are made by the online services in the voice section.
key.ph.replace: paste a new key to replace it
log.restarted: The server restarted; this job is gone.
run.restarted: Server restarted. Progress is saved — press Render to resume.
log.crashed: The server stopped responding mid-job — it most likely crashed (often the GPU: CUDA/cuDNN or out of memory).
run.crashed: The Folivox server crashed. See the terminal where folivox ui ran for the error; progress is saved — restart it and press Render to resume, or pick Device: cpu.
run.showing: Showing the job that is running on the server.
boot.fail: {msg} — open the link printed by folivox ui once (it contains the access token and sets a cookie).
engine.cosyvoice3.label: On this computer (CosyVoice 3)
engine.cosyvoice3.blurb: Free, private, works offline. Clones a voice from a short recording. Slower and the quality depends on your hardware.
engine.gemini.blurb: Google's voices: 30 ready-made ones, or describe a new voice in words (it exists only while the takes are made). Understands a note like 'calm audiobook narrator'. A free tier exists (Google may then use your text); the paid tier costs a fraction of a cent per sample.
engine.openai.blurb: 13 ready-made voices; a style note steers tone and pace ('audiobook narration, calm, steady pace'). No voice-from-description. Simple, reliable and cheap.
engine.elevenlabs.blurb: Very natural voices. Describe a new voice in words and get 3 different candidates at once, or pick a ready-made one. The free plan is for personal, non-commercial use; audiobooks you sell need a paid plan.
engine.cartesia.blurb: Clean, fast voices in 40+ languages. Pick a voice, give it the native accent of your book's language, or clone one of your own voices from your recording. No voice-from-description. Cloning needs a paid plan.
rv.sub: Every retake still differed from the text. Listen and compare with what speech recognition heard.
